text:
amy (eng): hi @people-ops — got a confusing denial. saw an ortho for wrist splint on 2026-04-02. Provider (Northside Orthopedics) shows as in-network in the carrier directory, but my EOB says 'facility billed out of network' and I owe the full amount. Claim# 864209300. i'm on the Premier plan. any quick tips?

dante (People Ops): sorry to hear that @amy. can you share the EOB photo or copy the line that shows the denial reason? also what member ID (last 4) is on the EOB?
amy (eng): EOB line: "Denied: Provider not contracted for billed place of service - facility billed as OON. Allowed $0.00, patient resp $220." Member ends 9912. Provider NPI on invoice: 5544332211.
sarah (Benefits): two likely causes: 1) the physician is in-network but the facility or billing tax ID is not (common when hospitals and physician groups bill separately), or 2) the claim was submitted under an affiliated outpatient surgery center NPI that isn't in-network. Do you have the billing provider name or TAX ID on the claim?
amy (eng): billing name shows "Northside Ortho Surgery Center" and TAX ID 12-3456789. Practice website lists the docs as in-network, but doesn't list the surgery center.
kevin (Health Plan Liaison): yep that aligns. If the rendering provider (the doctor) is in-network but the facility isn't contracted, carrier often treats entire claim as OON depending on plan language. We can: a) ask the provider to rebill splitting facility vs professional components or b) request a 'same or similar' review with carrier or c) check for surprise billing protections if service was emergent. Since this was scheduled, likely not emergency.
jules (Billing): ask the provider to re-file with separate line items: professional component (MD) and facility fee. Example request we send providers: ```service_date: 2026-04-02
claim_number: 864209300
member_last4: 9912
rendering_npi: 5544332211
billing_npi_facility: 6677889900
facility_tax_id: 12-3456789
line_items: CPT 29405 (splint) - professional fee; facility fee - UB04 codes as applicable
notes: please submit professional component under in-network group NPI and facility separately for reconsideration```
sarah (Benefits): @amy also check if you used the digital ID card at check-in. If the front desk used an old subscriber ID or typed a previous employer's group number, that can trigger OON processing. Does the EOB show the group number?
amy (eng): EOB group = 777-PREM. i did present the digital card but the receptionist said they typed my name differently. ugh.
dante (People Ops): @amy if you'd like us to liaise with the carrier, please upload the EOB + signed HIPAA release here: https://benefits.example.com/claims-portal and DM me the release. we'll open a carrier inquiry and request reprocessing if it's a billing provider mapping issue.
kevin (Health Plan Liaison): i'll open a carrier case once we have the docs. typical ask: re-evaluate eligibility for service date 2026-04-02 and re-adjudicate if facility and professional should be processed under in-network benefits. i'll request adjudication notes and the specific reason code.
jules (Billing): another tip: if provider refuses to split, we can request an administrative adjustment from the carrier attaching the provider's contract listing for the physician NPI. include the practice contract excerpt showing physician is in-network at that facility (if available).
hr-bot: Claim assistance FAQ & upload: https://benefits.example.com/claims-help. If claim is due to provider input error, Redwood policy may advance payment for covered amounts pending appeal for eligible employees — contact People Ops for pre-authorization.
amy (eng): i'll upload the EOB and DM the release now. also pinging the clinic billing mgr to ask about refiling. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
dante (People Ops): thanks @amy. once we have the release i'll open with carrier and cc provider. will update thread when carrier responds (SLA ~ 10 business days).
